reasons: Sources and market ranges are typed-in placeholders, yet the results are presented as researched citations.
Errors inside checks are silently replaced with empty results.
Confidence scores are hand-set numbers, not measured values.
No tests are visible in the files provided.
The context input and several settings are accepted or stored but never used.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file purpose
sections.what: Describes the file as a web research helper that checks inputs and outputs and gives citations. It brings in the libraries for web requests and HTML parsing, plus the shared data shapes for sources and results.
sections.why: Likely reason: the file was set up to fetch real web pages later, and the libraries are waiting for that work. Reason not fully stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Because the web libraries are imported but unused, the file looks like it fetches live data when it does not.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent (part 1)
sections.title: Agent setup and parallel checks
sections.what: Creates the agent with an optional API key and a few settings, but the key and settings are not used by the visible code. The research step then starts four checks at the same time: input checks, output checks, market tips and sources. A check that fails is replaced with an empty result, so the whole research still returns.
sections.why: Likely reason: running the checks together saves time, and empty fallbacks keep one failure from blocking the rest.
sections.watch_out: Failures are hidden, so an empty section looks the same as a check that found nothing to report.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent (part 2)
sections.title: Result build and cost input checks
sections.what: Packages the checks into one result object with a confidence score. It also compares the user's module, inverter and battery cost entries to market price ranges for those three components.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app and the Excel export need every check in one consistent shape. The reason for each fixed confidence value is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The confidence numbers for each check are typed in by hand, not measured.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent (part 3)
sections.title: Labor check and output benchmark check
sections.what: Checks the field labor rate against a market range. It then compares the calculated price for each component against a benchmark range. Each check returns a status and a confidence number.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app flags cost numbers that look out of line with market data.
sections.watch_out: The benchmark ranges are fixed numbers in a separate method, so every comparison here is only as good as those numbers.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent: _gather_market_insights
sections.title: Fixed market tips for each component
sections.what: Returns a fixed list of advice for each component, such as bifacial modules or LFP batteries, each with a short impact estimate. The text is written into the file and is not the result of any search.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The tax credit and cost figures in these tips are fixed text, so they will not update on their own.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent: _find_sources
sections.title: Fixed source list with citations
sections.what: Returns a fixed list of citations for each component. Each has a title, a web address, a quoted sentence, a relevance score and a timestamp. The code does not open any of these pages, and a comment says the list is mock data for now.
sections.why: The file comment says this is placeholder data until real searching is built, so the citations have not been checked.
sections.watch_out: These links and quotes look like real citations but were typed in by hand and never checked, so they must not be shown to users as verified sources.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent (part 6)
sections.title: Fixed price ranges and benchmarks
sections.what: Finishes the fixed source list. Then it returns a fixed price range for four input types and a fixed benchmark range for each component. These ranges are what user values are compared against.
sections.why: The file comments say these are mock ranges meant to be replaced by live data later.
sections.watch_out: An unknown input type gets a zero-to-zero range, which would make almost any value show as an error rather than unknown.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent: _determine_status
sections.title: Status, confidence and quote helpers
sections.what: Holds three small helpers. One turns a value and its range into a valid, warning or error label, with a 20 percent margin past the edges for warnings. One averages the confidence numbers from the checks and falls back to 0.8 when there are none. One takes the first three sources and turns them into quote entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: the result needs one status per check and one overall score. Reason for the 20 percent margin and the 0.8 fallback is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The overall confidence is a simple average of hand-typed numbers, so it reflects the code's guesses rather than the quality of the evidence.

sections.name: WebResearchAgent: research_all_components
sections.title: Research for all cost components
sections.what: Runs the research for eight components at once: modules, inverters, ess, sbos, ebos, labor, other and om. It pulls each component's inputs from the main cost inputs and its calculated values from the outputs. It keeps only the results that came back as proper research results.
sections.why: Likely reason: the whole cost model can be checked in one call, and a failed component does not stop the others.
sections.watch_out: The output lookup uses names such as modules, which may not match the names the calculator uses for its results, so a component may get no calculated values without any error.

sections.name: validate_input_field
sections.title: Check one input field alone
sections.what: Checks a single input value against the market range for its component. It creates a new agent each time it runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shortcut for checking one field without building a full research report.
sections.watch_out: The field name must match the names the input checks look for, or nothing is checked and the result is empty.

sections.name: get_market_insights
sections.title: Fetch market tips for one component
sections.what: Returns the fixed market tips for one component by creating a fresh agent and asking it for them.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets other parts of the app get tips without building an agent themselves.
sections.watch_out: Because a new agent is created each time, any future cache would start empty on every call.

sections.name: get_sources_for_component
sections.title: Fetch sources for one component
sections.what: Returns the fixed source list for one component, using a fresh agent.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as the tips function, a simple way for other code to get sources for one component.
sections.watch_out: The returned sources are the same hand-typed citations, and this function does not check the links.

summary: A research helper that compares user cost entries and calculated results against market ranges, then attaches tips and citations, but most of its market data and sources are fixed text typed into the file rather than fetched live.
purpose: Intended, according to the module description, to check inputs and outputs against current market data and to provide citations. Live data gathering is not implemented in this file.
why: The code comments say the data is mock data for now and that real lookups would be added later, so the file works as a stand-in until live research exists.
how: The research_component method starts four checks at the same time: input checks, output checks, market tips and source listing. It collects their results, replacing any failed check with an empty result, then computes an overall confidence score and quotes from the top sources. The research_all_components method runs this for eight cost components, and the small standalone functions run single parts on their own.
inputs: A component name such as modules, inverters, ess, sbos, ebos, labor, other or om. User cost inputs, as a dictionary or a full inputs object. Calculated results for that component. Optional text context, which is accepted but never used in the visible code.
outputs: A WebResearchResult object per component. It holds input checks (user value, market range, status and confidence), output checks, market tips, sources (title, link, quote and score), verbatim quotes and an overall confidence number. The research_all_components method returns a list of these results.
risks: The sources and market ranges are fixed text, so the results look researched when they are not. Errors inside checks are silently replaced with empty results, so an empty section looks like a passing check. Confidence numbers are typed in by hand. The timeout, source limit and cache settings are stored but not used, and the web libraries are imported but not used.
debug: If a component shows no checks, confirm its name matches one of the four components that have input checks, and confirm the calculated output keys match what this file expects. If results look too neat, remember the sources come from the _find_sources method and the ranges come from the _get_market_range method. To see hidden errors, temporarily log the exceptions that the gather step in research_component replaces.
